Hi Aisha / Dana — quick operational response below (bulleted). Happy to expand if Mark wants legal wording. I also attached the current subprocessors export and SOC2 summary.

Key custody / KMS:
- For Private VPC and on‑prem agent deployments we support customer‑managed keys. Customers may bring their own KMS (cloud KMS or on‑prem HSM) and configure the Redwood control plane and on‑prem agent to use customer keys for encryption of persisted model artifacts and customer data at rest.
- Key usage model: Redwood can be configured in two modes:
  1) Customer‑owned KMS: customer holds root keys; Redwood stores only key IDs and uses customer KMS endpoints for crypto operations (no plaintext keys stored by Redwood).
  2) Customer‑managed HSM connector: for on‑prem HSMs we support PKCS#11 integration; keys never leave the HSM.
- Escrow: We do not maintain a default key escrow. Escrow can be negotiated for enterprise contracts but requires explicit written agreement and separate escrow controls.

Data access & tenant isolation:
- Control plane: metadata required to route jobs (tenant id, model id, telemetry metadata) may transit Redwood control plane when using Redwood-hosted control plane for Private deployments. We can operate a customer‑managed control plane for large enterprise deals (see related_links for dataflow diagram).
- Dataplane / inference: inference workloads remain within customer VPC or on‑prem network; we do not persist customer prompts or outputs outside customer‑managed storage unless explicitly enabled (e.g., diagnostics traces).
- Tenant isolation: tenants are isolated logically; customer VPC/on‑prem agent model is single‑tenant for customer workloads — Redwood multi‑tenancy only applies to the hosted control plane services unless customer contracts a customer‑managed control plane.

Subprocessors and telemetry:
- Short list: cloud infra (GCP/Azure/AWS) for hosted control plane, monitoring provider (Datadog) for optional metrics, S3-compatible object storage vendors for backups (configurable). See attached subprocessors_list_20261119.csv for full list.
- We offer options to disable telemetry to the hosted control plane for customers who require minimal external egress.

Cross‑border transfers & data residency:
- By default control plane metadata may transit regions for routing and failover. Customers can request region restriction and address cross‑border concerns via contract terms. For EU data residency we can provision eu-central control plane nodes or provide a customer‑managed control plane.

Audit evidence & SOC2:
- We provided a SOC2 summary (soc2_summary_2026.pdf) and can provide scoped evidence on subprocessors during contract review.

Next steps:
- Aisha — I attached the subprocessors export and SOC2 summary. If FinLedger needs precise DPA clause language, Marissa and I can propose a short amendment (no more than 2 paragraphs) covering: (1) key custody, (2) no default escrow, (3) subprocessors and region restrictions.

Attachments: subprocessors_list_20261119.csv; soc2_summary_2026.pdf
